overview: White plays 1.g4, aiming a fianchettoed bishop at b7 down the long diagonal while giving up the g-pawn. After 1...d5 2.Bg2 Bxg4 3.c4 White hopes for play against d5 and b7, or a hit on the c6-square with Qb3. Most strong players take the pawn and White gets little for it; White's kingside is weakened by g4 and the line scores on surprise and traps.

white_ideas.idea: Bg2 hitting d5/b7, then c4 and Qb3 for pressure against Black's queenside
Surprise the opponent in unfamiliar play and hope for ...Bxg4 and a lead in development

black_ideas.idea: Take the g4 pawn with ...Bxg4 or ...e5 and ...d5 and develop freely
Hit the weakened kingside with ...h5 and use the open g-file and space in the centre

typical_structures.structure: White with a g2-bishop on the long diagonal and weakened kingside pawns, Black with an extra pawn and a big centre

character.notes: Unbalanced and risky for White with an exposed kingside; Sharp from Black's view too. Not known as a quiet line.

gambit.notes: After 1...d5 2.Bg2 Bxg4 3.c4 Black can keep the pawn; some lines (2.h3 e5) just weaken White without a gambit.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider it dubious for White; it works by surprise.

structure.notes: Flank opening where the centre is open for Black; Flexible with low confidence.

approach.notes: Anchor Offbeat: strong players hardly ever play it.

level.notes: A dubious line cannot be Beginner; Intermediate for White.

sublines_that_differ.name: 1...e5 2.d3
sublines_that_differ.how: No pawn is given; White plays a slow set-up, so no gambit.

character.reason: A weakened kingside and early tactics make it double-edged.

gambit.reason: The main 1...d5 2.Bg2 Bxg4 line gives a pawn White can't easily regain.

structure.reason: A flank opening with the centre undecided.

approach.reason: Seldom played by strong players, like the Grob in the anchors.

plans.reason: Bg2 on the long diagonal and quick development for a pawn.
